## Reply Argus, answered.

Everything you might want to know before you start. Still unsure? Just begin, the Free plan needs no card.

### What does Reply Argus do?

Reply Argus watches your App Store and Google Play reviews and drafts a reply to each one in your app's own voice. Both stores flow into a single inbox, every draft is grounded in facts about your app, and you either approve replies with a click or let the ones you trust publish on their own. It also clusters recurring feedback into a ranked list of what to fix and alerts you when a rating drops.

### Does it work with both the App Store and Google Play?

Yes. Reply Argus connects to both the Apple App Store and Google Play, and reviews from both land in one inbox. You reply to every review from a single place instead of tab-hopping between two consoles.

### What languages can it reply in?

100+ languages. Argus reads each review in the language it was written and replies in that same language with the tone intact, so a Japanese, German, or Portuguese reviewer gets a native-sounding answer, not a copy-paste translation.

### Is it safe to let it publish replies automatically?

Yes, because nothing publishes unless you tell it to. Approval mode is on by default: Argus drafts, you approve. Auto-publish is always opt-in and off by default, and on paid plans you can scope it precisely (5-star replies only, or by your own automation rules) so you decide exactly what is allowed to ship on its own.

### Is there a free plan?

Yes. The Free plan covers one active app with 100 replies a month across both stores, with manual approval and 5-star auto-publish. It is the only tool that lets you actually reply, for free. Paid plans start at $29/mo (Indie) and add the knowledge base, brand voice, ranked feedback, and instant alerts.

### How does Argus learn my brand voice?

It learns from your past approved replies plus everything it reads about your app on its own: your App Store and Play listings and your marketing page, pulled in automatically, kept separate per store. Every draft is grounded in those sources, each edit you make nudges the next draft closer to how you write, and if two sources contradict each other Argus flags it instead of guessing.

### Where do the replies get their facts?

From a per-app knowledge base Argus builds for you. Connect a store and it reads your App Store and Play listings and your marketing page on its own, and you can add your own notes, docs, and FAQs on top. Every draft is grounded in that knowledge and shows the exact lines it used, so a reply states real facts (your refund policy, your support link) instead of guessing, and it flags a mismatch when two sources disagree.

### Can it tell me what to fix next?

Yes, that is Signal. Argus clusters recurring requests and complaints across all your reviews into a ranked list of what to fix, each item backed by the real reviews behind it. Export the list one-way to Notion, Google Sheets, or a CSV, so your reviews stop being noise and become a prioritized roadmap.

### What else does it do beyond drafting replies?

It watches both stores continuously and alerts you in Slack, Telegram, Discord, email, or a webhook the moment a rating drops or a negative review lands. It gives you rating and response-rate analytics with an AI summary of the themes behind the numbers, reusable brand-voice profiles across a whole app portfolio, and a connector so you can run the whole review desk from Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client.
